column1: # S1 relay-seam manifest — the exact live W4-H1..H4 surface, re-enumerated from the command and
# agent bodies on 2026-08-17, not copied from audits/token-audit-2026-07-03-ai-resources.md § 4.
# Two audit step references did not survive re-enumeration and are corrected here: the
# execution-agent relay is wired at verify-chapter Step 2 (item 4), not Step 4 (which only logs),
# and evidence-to-report-writer is a SKILL loaded into a general-purpose subagent, not one of the
# One row per (seam, payload) pair. A seam that relays four artifact classes gets four rows, because
# each class is separately either intentional content or safely path-passable and each carries its
# The row does NOT record whether the seam currently complies. check-relay-payload.sh derives the
# current relay shape from the live `surface` file at `anchor`, so the check measures behaviour and
# reclassifies the moment a command body changes. A row asserting "noncompliant" would make the
# check unfalsifiable, which is the failure the S1 brief names explicitly.
#   class          W4-H1 | W4-H2 | W4-H3 | W4-H4  (audit finding class)
#   surface        file, relative to the workflow root
#   step           step/phase label as written in that file
#   anchor         ERE locating the ONE relay directive line; the matched line alone is the
#                  directive text the shape classifier reads (no multi-line bleed)
#   payload_token  literal naming this payload inside the directive text; the classifier reads the
#                  text immediately before and after the first match
#   list_intro     ERE locating the line that declares a multi-line relay list's convention, for
#                  bullet payloads whose own line carries no marker; `-` when not applicable
#   payload_glob   per-REPETITION fixture path(s), comma-separated, relative to fixture/
#   reps           repetitions across one section (per-chapter/per-cluster/per-session loops)
#   on_disk        yes | no  — does the payload already exist on disk when the relay happens
#   isolation      reference-path-ok    reference doc; required-reference-files.md § FX-C1 permits path
#                  operand-path-ok     bulk operand; the consumer can read it and no isolation rule binds it
#                  intentional-content per-chapter input the isolation contract passes by content
#                  ambiguous           the contract does not settle it — must not be guessed
#   blast_radius   live consumers carrying a copy of this surface
#   target         proposed contract: path | path+capped-summary | content-required
